blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The deployed MoCExchange is a verified proxy implementation, but the current whitelist set/controller state was not independently enumerated. The upstream arbitrary-account methods are therefore evidence of a candidate route, not confirmation that a currently whitelisted member can reach it in this deployment. The known MoC wrapper passes msg.sender (MoC.sol lines 316 and 335). Token/exchange proxy control makes Possible under the binding policy; whether a current whitelisted operator has an arbitrary-holder path remains unresolved.

oracleRisk.summary: Money On Chain's pooled rBTC system consumes the OMoC BTC/USD feed, where up to ten staked operators use off-chain quorum signatures and elected fallback publishers. An April 2026 consensus-bypass flaw prompted a protocol panic pause; the protocol's incident report states the bug was fixed.

branchApplicability.reviewer: OpenAI Codex external-a oracle applicability review
branchApplicability.rationale: Money On Chain has no borrower-specific collateral or liquidation branches, but its shared C0 system uses the BTC/USD oracle price to calculate DOC's rBTC mint/redemption conversion and global coverage state. That price-sensitive, system-wide conversion authority is therefore scored as a top-level control without inventing borrower branches.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: DOC is natively a Rootstock rBTC-collateralized CDP stablecoin. Its Arbitrum deployment (0x2ad62eb9...) is a self-deployed LayerZero V2 OFT representation documented by Money On Chain. Its low-supply Ethereum deployment is the legacy RSK Token Bridge eDOC SideToken (0x69f6d4d4...): at Ethereum block 25580192, the verified Bridge mapped original Rootstock token 0xe700691d... to eDOC in both directions. eDOC's sole minter was that Bridge proxy; upgrades and bridge ownership terminated at a 2-of-3 MultiSigWallet, while mint claims required the bridge's 2-of-5 Federation. Both peripheral deployments are external lock/mint routes rather than canonical rollup bridges.

protocols.name: Money On Chain — DOC on Arbitrum announcement (Stargate route)
protocols.note: Issuer states DOC moves Rootstock<>Arbitrum via Stargate (LayerZero), not a proprietary or canonical bridge.

protocols.name: Arbiscan — DOC Arbitrum token contract (LayerZero V2 OFT)
protocols.note: Verified contract 'MyOFT' on LZ endpoint 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c; owner-controlled peers/delegates, cross-chain mint/burn. Arbitrum supply is a minted OFT representation.

protocols.name: RSK Token Bridge — Ethereum eDOC SideToken and controller stack
protocols.note: Verified eDOC SideToken code assigns its sole minter to the RSK Bridge proxy. Fixed-block originalTokens(eDOC) and mappedTokens(Rootstock DOC) reads establish the canonical asset mapping; controller reads resolve a 2-of-3 admin multisig and a 2-of-5 claim federation.

protocols.name: Stargate Hydra docs (Pool-to-OFT lock/mint)
protocols.note: Hydra locks native asset on source chain (Protocol Locked Liquidity) and mints an OFT representation on the destination, an OFT-adapter lock/mint pattern.

routes.reviewNote: At Ethereum block 25580192, the verified Bridge's originalTokens(eDOC) returned Rootstock DOC 0xe700691d and mappedTokens(Rootstock DOC) returned eDOC, establishing the asset mapping on-chain. eDOC minter() returned Bridge proxy 0x12ed6935. The proxy implementation was 0x9f29f9bd and ProxyAdmin was 0xe4d35191; both ProxyAdmin.owner() and Bridge.owner() returned MultiSigWallet 0x040007b1 with required=2 and three owners. Bridge.getFederation() returned proxy 0x5e29c223, whose verified implementation required two votes from five enumerated members.
